claims.evidence: Retrieved text: an abnormal screening result is followed by colposcopy, with biopsies from suspicious areas.

Retrieved NHS text: specialist examines the cervix with a magnifying microscope with a light and may take a pin-head-sized tissue sample if something looks unusual; 'punch biopsy is common' was not stated.
claims.newSentence: Colposcopy is usually offered after an abnormal screening result: the cervix is looked at closely through a magnifying instrument, and a small tissue sample (biopsy) may be taken from anywhere that looks unusual.

claims.evidence: Hospital leaflet text: colposcopist decides between punch biopsies and a wire loop (LLETZ); cone biopsy removes a cone-shaped piece of tissue.
Retrieved leaflet text: punch biopsies are taken to confirm the diagnosis; colposcopy is an examination of the cervix.
Retrieved text: biopsy samples are examined by histology to confirm the diagnosis.
No retrieved NHS inform text gave this. Retrieved NHS text says cancer is found in rare cases; most abnormal findings are precancerous changes (CIN); 'very few require further treatment'.
claims.newSentence: Most findings at colposcopy are cell changes that are not cancer, and the NHS says cancer is found only in rare cases.

claims.evidence: Royal Marsden NHS page: staging work-up includes MRI, PET-CT and chest X-ray to find the extent (stage) of the cancer.

Retrieved: for stage 1A1 LLETZ or cone biopsy may remove all the cancer; radical hysterectomy is standard for early disease; radical trachelectomy keeps the uterus.

Retrieved CRUK/Macmillan text: radiotherapy mainly used for more advanced disease or when surgery is not suitable; chemotherapy or radiotherapy may follow surgery. 'Not fit for general anaesthetic' and 'reduce risk of coming back' were not retrieved.
claims.newSentence: Radiotherapy is mainly used for more advanced cancer or when surgery is not suitable, and chemotherapy or radiotherapy may be given after surgery.

claims.evidence: CRUK: chemoradiotherapy is the usual approach from stage 1B2 up to 4A; cisplatin is the most common drug.
CRUK: chemoradiotherapy most likely for stage 2B; may be suggested instead of surgery for some larger 2A tumours. 'Sometimes with surgery' was not retrieved.
claims.newSentence: For stage 2B, chemoradiotherapy is the most likely treatment, and for some larger stage 2A cancers it may be suggested instead of surgery.

claims.evidence: CRUK stage 4 page: pelvic exenteration (removal of pelvic organs) is offered to only a few people with stage 4A.

NICE TA939 recommends pembrolizumab with chemotherapy, with or without bevacizumab, for persistent, recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer (with a tumour test requirement); 'cancer that has spread' is too loose.
claims.newSentence: For cervical cancer that is persistent, has come back or has spread, NICE recommends the immunotherapy drug pembrolizumab with chemotherapy, with or without the targeted drug bevacizumab, for some adults.
